text:
sara: starting the planned tf apply for release/v2 now (change window). includes IAM role trust updates + tgw routing. tagging @dan @tara in case we need to hold.

deploybot: queued terraform apply (run-id: trf-8c3f). plan URL: https://ci.redwood/internal/runs/trf-8c3f 

dan: oncall here. quick question — the IAM drift alert from earlier this morning, is that related to these role trust docs?

sara: plan shows a trust policy replace on module.network.aws_iam_role.app_role: 
```
-  "AssumeRolePolicyDocument": {
-    "Statement": [ { "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/old-cross" } } ]
-  }
+  "AssumeRolePolicyDocument": {
+    "Statement": [ { "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/new-cross" } } ]
+  }
```
that new principal is the cross-account consumer in partner acct-222222. worried about breaking existing service principals that still assume the old ARN. Staging canary is green but it used a stubbed service in acct-222.

Also provider plugin: we pinned provider to 3.7.0 in staging but not prod. Recommend pinning provider in this run to avoid drift (provider override: registry.aws v3.7.0).

miles: we have the release cut at 17:30 UTC. can we do a staged apply: region-a first (rg1), wait 10m health checks, then region-b (rg2)? also add an automatic abort threshold: if >= 10% of requests to core-api 5xx within 5m after change, abort and rollback.

tara: security review — the policy change increases cross-account assume surface area. if we can't fully pause release, require a quick IAM-only rollback playbook ready: revert AssumeRolePolicyDocument to previous ARN and re-run apply for routing later. record IAM audit entries and rotate session tokens for service principals if needed.

deploybot: starting apply on module.network.rg1... logs: 
```
[apply] updating aws_iam_role.app_role (attempt 1)...
[apply] error: Error updating role: InvalidRequest: concurrent modification
```

sara: pausing the run. hitting concurrent modification on the IAM update. DO NOT proceed to rg2. I'm going to run a targeted revert for the IAM module to restore previous trust. command I'll run: 
```bash
# revert just the IAM role trust to previous state
git checkout HEAD~1 -- terraform/modules/network/iam_role.tf
terraform init -upgrade -get=false
terraform apply -target=module.network.aws_iam_role.app_role -auto-approve
```

dan: +1. hold Route53 / networking changes until we confirm the IAM role is stable. if the targeted apply fails, we escalate to emergency rollback: restore infra state to git sha <previous-sha> and run apply in maintenance window.

miles: copying to release notes & support: "Aborted prod infra apply — concurrent IAM update. Rolling back IAM trust to previous ARN. Networking/route53 changes delayed to next night window." pinging #support to watch for user reports. :loudspeaker:

tara: from security: after revert, run these checks before resuming: 1) IAM assume logs show successful AssumeRole calls for 24h 2) no auth failures in service accounts 3) rotate any session tokens if suspicious.

sara: done with targeted apply revert on rg1 — apply returned success for the role revert. will hold the rest and open a follow-up run tomorrow 01:00 UTC with provider pinned to 3.7.0, staged regions, 10m canary, and abort thresholds as discussed.

deploybot: run trf-8c3f marked paused; new run trf-8c3f-rollback completed. artifacts: https://ci.redwood/internal/runs/trf-8c3f-rollback 

dan: good. I'll mark the incident note and block the night run until we get signoff from security.

miles: thanks, team. I'll update the release timeline and note the delayed networking cut. reschedule attempt: 2026-03-21 01:00 UTC. :thumbsup:

sara: tagging oncall for that window @dan. we'll revalidate staging with provider pinned and run the IAM change as a separate, small canary first.

miles: closing thread — follow-up doc in #eng-releases with rollback steps and postmortem if any user impact is seen.
